To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Cramer-Raobound for the time-of-flight estimation problem is a lower bound on the variance of the estimator that is only valid if the dark noise and the photomultipler tube are perfect, and that for the problem of time-of-flight estimation of gamma rays using scintillation detectors the Cramer-Raubound is not valid for any realistic detector.
The Cramer-Rao lower bound on the time-of-flight error of scintillation detectors is not applicable for scintillation detectors with nearly exponential pulse shapes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new scintillation materials for the detection of ionizing radiation.
the development of a high resolution, low noise, high count rate detector for use with the next generation of gamma ray telescopes.
the development of a new generation of gamma ray detectors for the study of nuclear structure and astrophysics.
